label: rare: delimiter / first copy step in short sequences, often starting with u and containing k
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.03% of steps) that I could not pin to a selective predicate. 76% of activations and mass fall on the <DEL> step or the first copy step (recall_idx 0/1), but those steps are active only 0.15% of the time. Within them, rate goes up for short sequences (L=3-4), for first token u (15x lift; also d, v, digits), and when k shows up among the originals, especially as the last original token (prev2_tok=k, 12x). The top activations (~0.23) are sequences like u t k k <DEL> u. Even the best conjunctions reached only ~6% precision (F1 < 0.1). About 23% of the mass is at late original-phase steps (t=4-6) with no clear pattern. It never fires at t<3 or recall_idx>=2.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the input two steps back (most: k, a, m, p, y, r; least: s, -, i, u) and the current input token, by phase (copy phase: u, 0, 3, v; input phase: 0, 3, 2, w; delimiter step: <DEL>); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=1, t=5, L=3 & t=4.
